name: Lucy Williams
shortBio: Lucy is an independent consultant, accredited coach, and early years specialist with more than 20 years' experience leading national programmes in children's charities. She designs evidence-informed programmes that support parents of young children, with a particular focus on supporting families experiencing disadvantage. Lucy works with Family Hubs, local authorities, and charities to improve services and share best practice. She brings expertise in listening to children.
fullBio: Lucy Williams is an independent consultant and coach with 20 years' experience in national charities, leading and developing Home Learning Environment programmes that improve outcomes for young children and families. She has held senior leadership roles at Save the Children UK, the National Children's Bureau (NCB) and the National Literacy Trust. She is the Regional Lead for London for the National Centre for Family Hubs and has supported local authorities with the development of their Best Start in Life Plans and implementation strategies through her consultancy work at the Local Government Association.

Lucy generates meaningful collaboration through national partnerships with charities, the public sector, academics and funders. She is an experienced programme designer and manager with expertise across early years research, policy and practice and in co-design and listening to young children practice.

As Head of Early Years at Save the Children UK, Lucy led the development of the Early Years Knowledge Bank, an online resource focused on supporting babies and young children experiencing poverty in the UK. She also led the redevelopment of Families Connect, an evidence-based parental engagement programme that in 2025 she transitioned over to Peeple to become part of their portfolio. Lucy also led Save the Children UK's contribution to the COVID Inquiry (Module 8), examining the impact of the pandemic on children and young people in the UK.

At NCB, Lucy led the national rollout of Making it REAL (Raising Early Achievement in Literacy), now a Best Start in Life evidenced based programme. She also led the Young Children's Voices Network, working with 20 local authority partners to enable babies' and young children's perspectives to inform local decision-making.

Lucy has a teaching background (PGCE for Artists) and worked in gallery and museum education including in programme lead roles at Tate Modern and the Serpentine Gallery. She also delivered workshops for families, children and young people of all ages. Lucy trained in Sculpture at Chelsea Art School (BA Hons) and is a visual artist and an EMCC accredited professional coach (Level 5 qualification).
